name: M1151 HMMWV (armed), present day: the armoured body with the enclosed OGPK box turret and two whips

published.source: AM General / en.wikipedia 'Humvee': the M1114/M1151 family about 4.9 x 2.3 x 1.9 m on 37 in tyres, wheelbase 3.30 m (130 in). The length is not gated: the figure is rounded and does not say whether the pintle and the front shackles count (the model's 4.98 m X extent runs from the shackles to the pintle hook; [L1] puts the bumper face at x +2.18 and the tail at -2.38, 4.56 m of body).

engine_contract.row: js/eras.js / js/rules.js row nato_e00_recon; js/hero/us_humvee.js builds it through HeroHumvee.make(variant)
engine_contract.current_nodes: four 'roadwheel' groups (axle on local Y, origin on the axle) and one 'turret' group (origin on the ring, mast or slew ring, +X forward)
engine_contract.api: HeroHumvee.make(key)(THREE, M, C) is also called by js/hero/roc_retry.js (make('e00') for atgmv_r: it replaces the meshes of the 'turret' group and re-skins every material carrying userData.worldUV) and js/hero/roc_artillery.js (make('av') for roc_e90_spaag: re-skins the worldUV material); the skin keeps userData.worldUV = 4.6
engine_contract.len_rule: UNIT_MODELS[key].len = the measured X extent (atgmv_r in roc_retry.js keeps 4.98 on the e00 body, so the e00 extent may not move)

references.name: [L1] M1167 HMMWV (the M1151 armoured body) firing a TOW, Lithuania 2015, starboard broadside
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Bilateral wire guided missile training conducted in Lithuania 150806-A-FJ979-004.jpg' (US Army, public domain), 1200 x 534; cached in the scratchpad q_rocretry_ref by the M1167 builder
references.note: THE MEASURING PICTURE for the armoured body and for everything the HMMWV family shares (axles, tyres, the front clip, the arches). Near-square broadside from starboard (nose right), long lens. Scale on the 3.30 m wheelbase: hub centres at px (872.5, 441) and (406, 450), 466.5 px = 141.4 px a metre; the 9 px drop to the rear is a camera roll of 1.1 deg (rotate). Ground under each hub taken 0.47 m (the 37 in tyre) below it: the tyre feet are in grass, so every height carries about +-0.04 m of datum doubt and reads 0.03-0.06 m LOWER than the old file's [D1] drawing (roof 1.77 here, 1.87 there; published-family 1.83 for the M1025 on 36 in tyres) - the tolerances below are set to that doubt, not to the model. Outline hand-traced in this picture's pixels (b2_hmmwv/tools/mkspec.py), the ITAS turret above z 1.85 left out by window_m (this row carries the GPK / OGPK instead). Other trucks, dust and grass behind and under it: the trace, not a mask.

references.name: [R4] M1151 with the GPK and the M2 firing, Croatia, from astern
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Dog Company Trains in Croatia During Exercise DOG Custer (9866587).jpg' (US Army, DVIDS, public domain), 960 x 640; cached in the scratchpad q_rocretry_ref
references.note: For the reviewer: the GPK shield and its side wings from behind, the slant-back, the four 20 l jerrycans racked across the tail, the tail lamps, the pintle. Taken from above and behind: no scale.

references.name: [R2] M1097 Avenger, ROC Army, CKS Memorial Hall 2014, front-left
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'ROCA M1097 Avenger Display at CKS Memorial Hall Square 20140607.jpg' (CC BY-SA), 960 x 720; cached in the scratchpad q_rocart_ref
references.note: For the reviewer: the two-door hard cab of the M1097, the doors with the pressed X, the bonnet's raised intake on its left front, the turret on the bed - the low housing behind the cab, the two big pods of four on its sides (here raised), the gun and sight boxes under the right pod, two whips. Wears ROC camouflage and a number: the model is plain.

references.name: [R3] HMMWV front clip, ROC Army display (crop)
references.source: crop of a ROC Army display photograph cached in the scratchpad q_rk2_ref (crop_hmmwv.png; the source file name was not recorded by the builder who cut it)
references.note: For the reviewer: the grille face (vertical slots, the round headlamps inboard, amber lamps on the fender fronts), the chamfered fender tops, the RAISED AIR INTAKE - a box proud of the bonnet's left front quarter with its black grille - the windshield's two panes. Camouflage and number plate on it are not drawn. READING ONLY (review 1): its source file was not recorded, nothing is measured on it, and every feature cited is also in [R2], which the specs cite instead.

must_show: low and wide on four big 37 in tyres at the corners, axles at x +1.65 and -1.65, the tyres standing out under full-width fenders (half width 1.15 m)
the one-piece front clip: bonnet sloping from z 1.25 at the cowl (x 0.96) to 1.03 at the nose (x 2.16), chamfered outer fender tops, the square-topped wheel openings with their tops at z 0.96
the grille face at x 2.19: vertical slots between the two round headlamps, the amber lamps on the fender fronts outboard [R2]
the RAISED AIR INTAKE on the bonnet's left front quarter, x 1.41..2.03, y +0.06..+0.60, about 6 cm proud with its black slatted grille [R2]
the intake stack up the right of the windshield at x 0.88, y -1.02, from the fender top to a cap at z 1.80 [L1]
the near-upright armoured windshield in a heavy black frame, its foot at the cowl x 0.94 and its top at the roof front x 0.76 [L1]

four thick flat armoured doors with seams at x 0.70, -0.20 and -1.12, their outside hinges and black D-ring pulls (z 0.72), small armour windows in a black gasket inside wide raised bolted frames (front glass x 0.05..0.56, rear -1.00..-0.41, z 1.25..1.50) [L1]
the bolted armour plate on the body side behind the front wheel, x 0.73..1.19, z 0.42..0.94 [L1]

the flat roof at z 1.78 to x -1.12, then the bare slant-back to the tail top at z 1.40 (x -2.36): the seam round its rear lid, the two black blocks at its top corners (x -1.38..-1.10), the thin ledge across it half way down (x -1.81, at most 1.5 cm proud), the edge bolts [L1][R4]; the roof's plain edge rails with four bolts a side and a black slot near x -0.28 [L1]
the dark louvred panel on each rear quarter in a raised frame, x -2.26..-1.42, z 1.03..1.19 [L1]
the geared hubs: the wheel face with its eight nuts and the hub cap turning with the tyre, the painted rims (all four wheels, centres z 0.47)
the jerrycan rack across the tail, four cans at z 0.70..1.17, and the big black rear mudflaps behind the rear wheels (x -2.31, z 0.10..0.62) [R4]
plain CARC tan, no markings: darker under the belt line (z < 1.1), dried mud to z 0.6 and splashed round both arches (x +-1.65), dust on the bonnet and roof

the OGPK box turret on the ring at x -0.35: armoured lower walls, glass bands between four corner posts, a roof over its front half and the rear half open over the gunner, the M2 out of the front; a second whip on the left rear (x -1.10, y +1.02)
